intended_object: Given index subsets S ⊆ T, this is the R-linear map ⨁_{i∈S} M_i → ⨁_{i∈T} M_i that sends each summand M_i (i ∈ S) to the same summand in the larger sum. The meaning comes from the docstring and from the analogous `DirectSum.setToSet`.
explanation:
The definition is the faithful linear version of the inclusion of a partial direct sum into a larger one. The body uses the universal property `toModule` and sends the summand for i ∈ S to the summand for ⟨i, H i.prop⟩ ∈ T through `lof`. On each component this is exactly the canonical inclusion, and `toModule` extends it linearly, as it should.

The generality is the natural one: R is any semiring, the M_i are any family of R-modules and ι is any index type. `DecidableEq ι` is only the usual technical assumption in the direct-sum API.

`DirectSum.setToSet` in `Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean` is the same construction as an additive monoid homomorphism (`→+`). This definition is its R-linear counterpart, not a narrower copy of it.
